symbols.name: D
symbols.def: Number of observed variables.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Number of non-observational regimes.

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: A finite set of selection vertices disjoint from \(V\).

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: \(X=(X_v)_{v\in V}\) is the observed reality-world random vector, with every \(\mathcal X_v\) finite.

symbols.name: S_star
symbols.def: \(S^*=(S_s^*)_{s\in S}\) is the counterfactual basal-world selection-status vector; a unit is observed exactly on \(S^*=\mathbf 1\).

symbols.name: zeta
symbols.def: \(\zeta=(\zeta_1,\ldots,\zeta_K)\) are distinct regime-indicator vertices disjoint from \(V\cup S\); \(\zeta_k\) is included only in regime \(k\)'s MAG.

symbols.name: U_k
symbols.def: \(U_k\) is the full observed-plus-indicator vertex domain of regime \(k\)'s MAG; \(U_0\) has no intervention indicator.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: For each selected-intervention model \(g\in\mathcal G_{D,K}\), \(T(g)=(T_1(g),\ldots,T_K(g))\) is its latent family of direct soft-intervention targets.

symbols.name: G0
symbols.def: For a model tuple \(g\in\mathcal G_{D,K}\), \(G_0(g)\) is its basal selected DAG on the disjoint vertex union \(V\cup S\).

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: For \(g\in\mathcal G_{D,K}\), \(\kappa_v^{(j)}(g)(dx_v\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_{G_0(g)}(v)})\) is the regime \(j\) local kernel at vertex \(v\); the collection factors the joint basal or intervention law over \(G_0(g)\).

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: \(\eta=(S,G_0(\eta),(T_k(\eta))_{k=1}^{K},(\kappa^{(j)}(\eta))_{j=0}^{K})\). The kernels factor over the common basal selected DAG \(G_0(\eta)\); \(\kappa_v^{(k)}(\eta)=\kappa_v^{(0)}(\eta)\) for every \(v\notin T_k(\eta)\); and the common selection event has positive probability, \(\Pr_{\eta}(S^*=\mathbf 1)>0\). Conditioning the factored arm laws on this event induces \(P_{\eta}^{(0)},\ldots,P_{\eta}^{(K)}\) and their pooled binary-indicator laws.

symbols.name: P_sel
symbols.def: \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}\) is the selected pure-observational law \(p_{\eta}(X\mid\zeta_k=0,S^*=\mathbf 1)\), common to every comparison \(k\in[K]\), and \(P_{\eta}^{(k)}\) is the selected intervention law \(p_{\eta}(X\mid\zeta_k=1,S^*=\mathbf 1)\).

symbols.name: P_pool
symbols.def: \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) is the equal-weight joint law of \((X,\zeta_k)\) obtained by pooling the selected observational arm \(p_{\eta}(X\mid\zeta_k=0,S^*=\mathbf 1)\) and selected intervention arm \(p_{\eta}(X\mid\zeta_k=1,S^*=\mathbf 1)\).

symbols.name: M_DK
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), defined in \(\mathrm{def:model-class}\).

symbols.name: M_k
symbols.type: ordered maximal ancestral graph family map
symbols.def: \(M_0(\eta)\) is the observational latent projection on \(U_0=V\). For \(k\in[K]\), \(M_k(\eta)\) is the latent projection on \(U_k=V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) of the interventional twin graph whose observed law is the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\).

symbols.name: O
symbols.def: \(\mathcal O(\eta)=\bigl(\operatorname{skel}(M_k(\eta)),\operatorname{UC}(M_k(\eta))\bigr)_{k=0}^{K}\), where both components are taken on the full regime domain \(U_k\). For every \(k\in[K]\), \(M_k(\eta)\) is interpreted through the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), not through either arm law alone, and the signature retains every adjacency and every unshielded collider involving only vertices in \(V\) or involving \(\zeta_k\).

symbols.name: C_O
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)=\{\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}:\mathcal O(\eta)=\mathcal O\}\).

symbols.name: E_O
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\) contains the endpoint positions on observed--observed adjacencies of the full MAGs \(M_k(\eta)\), \(k=0,\ldots,K\). Endpoints at \(\zeta_k\) are retained in \(\mathcal O\) as constraints on the fiber but are excluded from this reported endpoint domain.

symbols.name: mu
symbols.def: \(\mu_\eta(e)\) is the endpoint mark at the observed endpoint position \(e\) in the corresponding induced graph \(M_k(\eta)[V]\).

symbols.name: P_SI
symbols.def: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\) records, on \(\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\), the observed-endpoint mark common to all \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), and a circle otherwise. The compatibility fiber is defined by the complete \(U_k\)-level adjacency and unshielded-collider signatures of the pooled selected laws \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving constraints.

symbols.name: O_0
symbols.def: \(\mathcal O_0(\eta)=\mathcal I(M_0(\eta))\) is the full set of conditional-independence relations encoded by the observational MAG on \(V\); it therefore fixes the complete observational Markov-equivalence class used by Zhang's PAG.

symbols.name: E_0
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_0(\mathcal O_0)\) contains the two endpoint positions of every adjacency common to the observational Markov-equivalence class indexed by \(\mathcal O_0\).

symbols.name: C_MAG0
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MAG}}(\mathcal O_0)=\{M\in\operatorname{MAG}(V):\mathcal I(M)=\mathcal O_0\}\).

symbols.name: C_Dai0
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Dai}}(\mathcal O_0)=\{M_0(\eta):\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,0}^{\mathrm{Dai}},\ \mathcal O_0(\eta)=\mathcal O_0\}\).

symbols.name: nu
symbols.def: \(\nu_M(e)\) is the endpoint mark at \(e\) in an observational MAG \(M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MAG}}(\mathcal O_0)\).

symbols.name: P_Zhang
symbols.def: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{Z}}(\mathcal O_0)\) records an endpoint mark when \(\nu_M\) has that mark for every \(M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MAG}}(\mathcal O_0)\), and records a circle otherwise.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: For each model \(\eta\), \(A(\eta)=\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta)}(\operatorname{pa}_{G_0(\eta)}(S))\cap V\), including the observed selection parents.

symbols.name: C_fixA
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\widetilde\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O):A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)\}\).

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: \(F_k(\eta)\) is the set of observed variables directly or indirectly affected by regime \(k\)'s direct target set \(T_k(\eta)\).

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: The observational skeleton in \(\mathcal O\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: \(Z=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_K)\), where \(Z_k=\operatorname{adj}_{M_k(\eta)}(\zeta_k)\cap V\), is read from the full signature \(\mathcal O\). By Dai et al.'s Lemma 5, \(Z_k=T_k(\eta)\cup((F_k(\eta)\setminus T_k(\eta))\cap A(\eta))\); hence \(Z_k\) contains direct targets together with any indirectly affected ancestrally selected variables and need not equal \(T_k(\eta)\).

symbols.name: sigma
symbols.def: \(\sigma(v)=\{k\in[K]:v\in Z_k\}\).

symbols.name: L_A
symbols.def: \(x\to y\in L_{A(\eta)}\) iff \(xy\in H[A(\eta)]\) and \(\sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\).

symbols.name: Reach_A
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(x,y)=1\) iff \(L_{A(\eta)}\) contains a nonempty directed path from \(x\) to \(y\).

symbols.name: C_sel
symbols.def: \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\) is the least observable vertex set defined in \(\mathrm{def:observable\mbox{-}selectedness\mbox{-}closure}\).
symbols.role: observable surrogate for certified selection membership

symbols.name: L_cert
symbols.def: \(x\to y\in L_{\mathrm{cert}}(\mathcal O)\) if and only if \(xy\in H[\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)]\) and \(\sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\).

symbols.name: Reach_cert
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathrm{cert},\mathcal O}(x,y)=1\) if and only if \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}(\mathcal O)\) contains a nonempty directed path from \(x\) to \(y\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: An acyclic signature-monotone subgraph of \(H[A(\eta)]\) with no new unshielded collider.

symbols.name: RepGraph
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) is the purely graphical replacement specification constructed in \(\mathrm{def:basal\mbox{-}replacement}\); it contains a basal selected DAG and direct-target sets but no probability kernels.

symbols.name: Real
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)=\{\widetilde\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}:(G_0(\widetilde\eta),(T_k(\widetilde\eta))_{k=1}^{K})=\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\}\). Membership fixes only the replacement graph and direct-target data; every member carries its own fully specified kernel family.

symbols.name: G_san
symbols.def: \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{san}}\) is the explicit \(D=3\), \(K=1\) graph-and-target specification in \(\mathrm{def:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}specification}\).

symbols.name: Lambda_SI
symbols.def: The admissible fixed endpoint-rule grammar in \(\mathrm{def:rule-language}\).

symbols.name: Hdl_SI
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{Hdl}_{\mathrm{SI}}\) is the observable synchronized Zhang--Dai rule-development handle in \(\mathrm{def:calculus-handle}\).

symbols.name: R_SI
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) is the finite rule list derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:selection-lifting}\).

symbols.name: Cl_R
symbols.def: Least monotone closure of reported observed endpoints under \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\), with the complete pooled-law \(U_k\)-level skeleton and unshielded-collider signature used as fixed premises.

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(\mathcal Q\) contains every finite-alphabet query needed to recover \(\mathcal O\). An observational or intervention-arm CI query \(q=(R_1,R_2\mid W;j)\), \(j\in\{0,\ldots,K\}\), is evaluated from \(P_{\eta}^{(j)}\), but is interpreted as the corresponding conditional slice \(X_{R_1}\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X_{R_2}\mid X_W,\zeta_k=z\) of a pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), with \(z=0\) for \(j=0\) and \(z=1\) for \(j=k\); no arm law is separately assumed faithful. For every \(k\in[K]\), an indicator query \(q=(\zeta_k,X_R\mid X_W;k)\) is evaluated under \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) and is equivalent to equality of \(p_{\eta}(X_R\mid X_W,\zeta_k=0,S^*=\mathbf 1)\) and \(p_{\eta}(X_R\mid X_W,\zeta_k=1,S^*=\mathbf 1)\). Jointly these queries determine every adjacency and unshielded collider on each \(U_k\), including every instance involving \(\zeta_k\).

symbols.name: I_Q
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_{\mathcal Q}\) contains every pair \((q,w)\) for which query \(q\in\mathcal Q\) conditions on the realized finite-alphabet stratum \(w\), with the single dummy stratum \(w=\varnothing\) of mass one for an unconditional query.

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: \(\rho(q,w)\) is the probability of conditioning stratum \(w\) under \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}\) for an observational query and under \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) for a paired query indexed by \(k\).

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: For an arm-CI query \(q=(R_1,R_2\mid W;j)\), let \(p_q\) be the selected-arm finite table and let \(\mathcal N_q\) be the conditional-independence null \(X_{R_1}\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X_{R_2}\mid X_W\). For an indicator query \(q=(\zeta_k,X_R\mid X_W;k)\), let \(p_q\) be the ordered pair of selected conditional tables induced by \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), and let \(\mathcal N_q\) be equality of the \(\zeta_k=0\) and \(\zeta_k=1\) kernels. Define \(\Gamma(q)=\inf_{r\in\mathcal N_q}\lVert p_q-r\rVert_1\), using the sum \(\ell_1\) norm for an ordered pair. Thus \(\Gamma(q)/2\) is the corresponding total-variation distance.

symbols.name: a_max
symbols.def: \(a_{\max}\) is the maximum number of cells in any joint finite-alphabet table indexed by one query in \(\mathcal Q\).

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: \(n=(n_0,\ldots,n_K)\) gives the independent sample size in each regime.

symbols.name: p_min
symbols.def: \(p_{\min}\) is the lower bound on every conditioning-stratum probability queried by \(\mathcal Q\).

symbols.name: Delta
symbols.def: \(\Delta\) is a lower bound on every nonzero \(\ell_1\) contrast \(\Gamma(q)\), \(q\in\mathcal Q\); one half of this contrast is the corresponding total-variation distance.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Simultaneous graph error level \(\alpha\).

symbols.name: B_mc
symbols.def: \(B_{\mathrm{mc}}\) is the number of independent Monte Carlo permutations used for each conditional-independence query.

symbols.name: d_hat
symbols.def: \(\widehat d(q)=0\) denotes acceptance of the CI or invariance null indexed by \(q\), and \(\widehat d(q)=1\) denotes rejection, under the calibration in \(\mathrm{def:confidence\mbox{-}si\mbox{-}pag}\).

symbols.name: E_Q
symbols.def: \(\mathsf E_{\mathcal Q}=\{\widehat d(q)=\mathbf 1\{\Gamma(q)>0\}\text{ for every }q\in\mathcal Q\}\) is the uniform query-recovery event.

symbols.name: O_hat
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\mathcal O}\) is the collection of the observational signature recovered from queries under \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}\) and every full paired-regime skeleton and unshielded-collider signature on \(U_k\) recovered from queries under \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), including all indicator adjacencies and all indicator-involving unshielded colliders.

symbols.name: P_conf
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\mathcal P}_{\mathrm{conf}}=\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\widehat{\mathcal O})\).

assumptions.condition: \(G_0(\eta)\) is a finite directed acyclic graph on the disjoint union \(V\cup S\).
No latent variable is a common cause of two vertices in \(V\).
Every node in \(S\) is childless in \(G_0(\eta)\) and has all parents in \(V\).
The event determined by \(S\) is generated in the basal world before every regime indexed by \(T(\eta)\).

For every comparison \(k\in[K]\), the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}(dx,dz)=\tfrac12p_{\eta}(dx\mid\zeta_k=0,S^*=\mathbf 1)\delta_0(dz)+\tfrac12p_{\eta}(dx\mid\zeta_k=1,S^*=\mathbf 1)\delta_1(dz)\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) is faithful to \(M_k(\eta)\): for every disjoint vertex sets \(R_1,R_2,W\subseteq U_k\), \(X_{R_1}\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X_{R_2}\mid X_W\) under \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) if and only if \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) are \(m\)-separated by \(W\) in \(M_k(\eta)\), with \(X_{\zeta_k}:=\zeta_k\).
For each \(k\in\{0,\ldots,K\}\), the \(n_k\) observations are independent draws from regime \(k\), and the regime samples are mutually independent.

novel.justification: This maintained finite-table overlap condition is realistic when the query family excludes structurally empty or scientifically irrelevant rare strata; it permits arbitrarily heterogeneous positive stratum masses above the declared floor.

definitions.name: Published common-basal selected-intervention class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}=\{\eta=(S,G_0(\eta),(T_k(\eta))_{k=1}^{K},(\kappa^{(j)}(\eta))_{j=0}^{K})\in\mathcal G_{D,K}: D\in\mathbb N_+,\ K\in\mathbb N_0,\ \eta\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:basal\mbox{-}dag},\mathrm{ass:causal\mbox{-}sufficiency},\mathrm{ass:selection\mbox{-}structure},\mathrm{ass:pretreatment\mbox{-}selection},\mathrm{ass:soft\mbox{-}intervention},\mathrm{ass:twin\mbox{-}faithfulness}\}\). Here the kernels factor over \(G_0(\eta)\), satisfy \(\kappa_v^{(k)}(\eta)=\kappa_v^{(0)}(\eta)\) for \(v\notin T_k(\eta)\), assign positive probability to \(S^*=\mathbf 1\), and induce the selected arm and pooled laws after conditioning on that common event.

definitions.name: Full oracle regime-MAG signature
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O(\eta)=\bigl(\operatorname{skel}(M_k(\eta)),\operatorname{UC}(M_k(\eta))\bigr)_{k=0}^{K}\), with both operators evaluated on all of \(U_k\). For each \(k\in[K]\), the conditional-independence input is that of the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\), whose two arm laws are \(p_{\eta}(X\mid\zeta_k=0,S^*=\mathbf 1)\) and \(p_{\eta}(X\mid\zeta_k=1,S^*=\mathbf 1)\). Thus the signature includes every adjacency \(\zeta_k-v\) and every unshielded collider whose triple contains \(\zeta_k\), as well as every adjacency and unshielded collider entirely within \(V\).

definitions.name: Common-basal compatibility fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)=\{\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}:\bigl(\operatorname{skel}(M_k(\eta)),\operatorname{UC}(M_k(\eta))\bigr)_{k=0}^{K}=\mathcal O\}\). Each member supplies, for every \(k\in[K]\), the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) faithful to \(M_k(\eta)\); neither arm law is substituted for this pooled law. Equality preserves every adjacency and every unshielded collider on each full domain \(U_k\), including all indicator-involving instances.

definitions.name: Canonical endpoint-invariance SI-PAG
definitions.construction: For each reported observed endpoint \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\), set \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=m\) if \(\mu_\eta(e)=m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\) for every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), and set \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}\) otherwise. The fiber \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) is constrained by the full regime-MAG signatures induced by the pooled selected laws \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(U_k\), including indicator adjacencies and indicator-involving unshielded colliders, even though endpoints at \(\zeta_k\) are not part of the reported graph.

definitions.name: Fixed ancestral-selection compatibility fiber
definitions.construction: For \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), define \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\widetilde\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O):A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)\}\).

definitions.name: Full observational Markov-equivalence input
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O_0(\eta)=\mathcal I(M_0(\eta))\), where \(\mathcal I(M)\) is the complete set of conditional-independence relations entailed by \(m\)-separation in \(M\).

definitions.name: Zhang observational PAG
definitions.construction: For each \(e\in\mathcal E_0(\mathcal O_0)\), set \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm Z}(\mathcal O_0)(e)=m\) if \(\nu_M(e)=m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\) for every \(M\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MAG}}(\mathcal O_0)\), and set \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm Z}(\mathcal O_0)(e)=\mathtt{circle}\) otherwise.

definitions.name: Signature-monotone selected graph
definitions.construction: For each \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), \(L_{A(\eta)}=(A(\eta),\{x\to y:xy\in H[A(\eta)],\ \sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\})\), with \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(x,y)\) the nonempty directed reachability relation in \(L_{A(\eta)}\).

definitions.name: Observable selectedness-certificate closure
definitions.construction: Let \(C^{(0)}(\mathcal O)\subseteq V\) contain both observed endpoints of every observed--observed adjacency that is absent from the observational skeleton \(H\) and present in at least one intervention-regime skeleton in \(\mathcal O\). Recursively, let \(C^{(r+1)}(\mathcal O)\) equal \(C^{(r)}(\mathcal O)\) together with every middle vertex \(x\) of an observational unshielded noncollider \(i-x-j\) whose nonadjacent endpoints \(i,j\) lie in \(C^{(r)}(\mathcal O)\). Define \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)=\bigcup_{r=0}^{|V|}C^{(r)}(\mathcal O)\), \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}(\mathcal O)=(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O),\{x\to y:xy\in H[\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)],\ \sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\})\), and let \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathrm{cert},\mathcal O}\) be nonempty directed reachability in this graph. Every ingredient is computed from \(\mathcal O\); no compatible model or latent set \(A(\eta)\) is queried.

definitions.name: Selected-subgraph replacement
definitions.construction: Given \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), define \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)=(\widetilde G_0,(\widetilde T_k)_{k=1}^{K})\) as follows. Replace the basal edge set by \(\bigl(E(G_0(\eta))\setminus E(G_0(\eta)[A(\eta)])\bigr)\cup E(B)\), add a childless pair-parent selection node for every edge of \(H[A(\eta)]\), and add a singleton-parent selection node for every vertex of \(A(\eta)\). For each \(k\in[K]\), retain \(T_k(\eta)\setminus A(\eta)\) and let \(\widetilde T_k\cap A(\eta)\) be the ancestry-minimal generators of \(Z_k\cap A(\eta)\) in \(\widetilde G_0\): \(v\in Z_k\cap A(\eta)\) is included exactly when it is not a proper descendant of another vertex of \(Z_k\cap A(\eta)\) or of a retained exterior direct target. This construction specifies only \(\widetilde G_0\) and \(\widetilde T_k\); it assigns no kernels and does not designate a replacement model.

definitions.name: Fully specified replacement realization fiber
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)=\{\widetilde\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}:(G_0(\widetilde\eta),(T_k(\widetilde\eta))_{k=1}^{K})=\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\}\). The defining predicate fixes the graphical and target components only; the kernel family \(\kappa(\widetilde\eta)\) is part of each fully specified member and is not inherited from \(\eta\).

definitions.name: Retained-edge sanity specification
definitions.construction: Set \(D=3\), \(K=1\), \(V=\{1,2,3\}\), and \(S=\{s\}\). Define \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{san}}\) by the basal selected DAG \(E(G_0)=\{1\to2,2\to s\}\), with vertex \(3\) isolated in the basal DAG, and the direct soft-intervention target \(T_1=\{3\}\). No other basal edge or direct target is present.

definitions.name: Fixed SI endpoint-rule grammar
definitions.construction: \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\) is the grammar of monotone endpoint rules with finitely many typed vertex and regime placeholders. Premises may use any adjacency or unshielded-collider predicate in the complete \(U_k\)-level signature \(\mathcal O\), where every \(k\in[K]\) input is the signature of the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), including predicates whose vertices contain \(\zeta_k\), together with current observed-endpoint, uncovered-path, discriminating-path, membership in the observable certificate set \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\), and reachability in \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}(\mathcal O)\); conclusions replace reported observed circles by tails or arrowheads. No rule premise may mention \(A(\eta)\), \(L_{A(\eta)}\), a member of \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), a realizability oracle, or a model enumerator.

definitions.name: Observable synchronized Zhang--Dai construction handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Hdl}_{\mathrm{SI}}\): start from Zhang's rules R0--R10 applied to each full regime signature on \(U_k\), interpreting the \(k\)-th signature as that of the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\). Compute \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\) from intervention-created adjacencies and observational-unshielded-noncollider closure, then propagate forbidden signature transitions only along shortest uncovered paths certified by \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathrm{cert},\mathcal O}\). Enforce Dai et al.'s Lemma 5 disjunction \(Z_k=T_k(\eta)\cup((F_k(\eta)\setminus T_k(\eta))\cap A(\eta))\) only as a witness obligation, without identifying \(T_k(\eta)\) with \(Z_k\). Use \(L_{A(\eta)}\), \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\), and \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) only in the completeness proof to extend or oppose marks after an observable rule fires; none is a rule premise. The handle derives the finite list in \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\) from observable predicates alone.

definitions.name: Rule closure
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\) is initialized with every skeleton and every unshielded collider in the complete regime-MAG signatures on \(U_k\), with each non-observational signature supplied by \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) and including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances. It treats this full input signature as immutable premises and repeatedly applies every instance of every rule in \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) until no reported observed circle endpoint changes.

definitions.name: Finite-alphabet confidence SI-PAG
definitions.construction: For an arm-CI query \(q=(R_1,R_2\mid W;j)\), use the selected-arm sample from \(P_{\eta}^{(j)}\) to evaluate the corresponding conditional slice of a pooled law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\); this does not impose faithfulness on \(P_{\eta}^{(j)}\) itself. Apply the UCI statistic of Kim et al., Section 4.2, Algorithm 2, permuting the second queried variable independently within each realized \(W\)-stratum. From \(B_{\mathrm{mc}}\) independent permutations set \(p_q^{\mathrm{mc}}=(1+\sum_{b=1}^{B_{\mathrm{mc}}}\mathbf 1\{T_q^{(b)}\ge T_q\})/(B_{\mathrm{mc}}+1)\). For an indicator query \(q=(\zeta_k,X_R\mid X_W;k)\), compare the two selected conditional multinomial tables \(p_{\eta}(X_R\mid X_W,\zeta_k=0,S^*=\mathbf 1)\) and \(p_{\eta}(X_R\mid X_W,\zeta_k=1,S^*=\mathbf 1)\) with simultaneous cell-probability bands; this is the \(\zeta_k\)-conditional-independence null under \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\). Allocate querywise type-I and type-II errors \(\alpha_q=\beta_q=\alpha/(2|\mathcal Q|)\), use \(\widehat d(q)=1\) when the calibrated test rejects, construct \(\widehat{\mathcal O}\) from every pooled-law skeleton and unshielded-collider decision on \(U_k\), including every indicator adjacency and every indicator-involving unshielded collider, and return \(\widehat{\mathcal P}_{\mathrm{conf}}=\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\widehat{\mathcal O})\) on reported observed endpoints. Under an arm-CI null, the observed and within-stratum permuted statistics are exchangeable, so the Monte Carlo \(p\)-value is super-uniform. Kim et al., Section 4.2, Theorem 2, and its proof in Appendix C.2 use a Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz comparison between the Monte Carlo and full permutation quantiles to retain the fixed-alphabet \(\ell_1\)-separation sample order. For tables with at most \(a_{\max}\) cells and conditioning-stratum mass at least \(p_{\min}\), multinomial concentration gives simultaneous contrast error of order \(\sqrt{\log(2|\mathcal Q|/\alpha)/(p_{\min}\min_{0\le j\le K} n_j)}\); the displayed sample bound makes this smaller than a fixed fraction of \(\Delta\). A union bound over querywise type-I and type-II failures yields \(\mathsf E_{\mathcal Q}\).

statements.statement: Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\). If \(B\) is acyclic, every edge of \(B\) lies in \(H[A(\eta)]\), \(B\) creates no unshielded collider whose endpoints are nonadjacent in \(H\), and every \(x\to y\in B\) satisfies \(\sigma(x)\subseteq\sigma(y)\), then the basal DAG \(\widetilde G_0\) in \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{An}_{\widetilde G_0}(\operatorname{pa}_{\widetilde G_0}(S))\cap V=A(\eta)\). For every \(k=0,\ldots,K\), the twin graph determined by \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) has a latent-projection MAG on \(U_k\) with exactly the adjacency and unshielded-collider signature of \(M_k(\eta)\), including every adjacency and every unshielded collider involving \(\zeta_k\). For \(k\in[K]\), its target and descendant data realize \(Z_k=\widetilde T_k\cup((\operatorname{de}_{\widetilde G_0}(\widetilde T_k)\cap V\setminus\widetilde T_k)\cap A(\eta))\), with the two terms representing direct targets and indirectly affected ancestrally selected vertices separately.
statements.justification: This lemma isolates the graph-theoretic obligation: the replacement specification preserves the full oracle signature before any probability law is chosen.
statements.gap: Dai et al. characterize equivalence but do not give a synchronized common-basal graph replacement preserving every indicator-involving signature constraint.
statements.consumer: It supplies the graphical half of each opposing selected-endpoint witness used by the complete calculus.

statements.statement: Under the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\), there exist finite-alphabet local kernels \(\widetilde\kappa=(\widetilde\kappa_v^{(j)})_{v\in V\cup S,\ 0\le j\le K}\) factoring over the basal DAG in \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\), satisfying \(\widetilde\kappa_v^{(k)}=\widetilde\kappa_v^{(0)}\) for every \(v\notin\widetilde T_k\), and assigning positive probability to \(S^*=\mathbf 1\), such that the resulting fully specified model \(\widetilde\eta\) belongs to \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\). Simultaneously for every \(k\in[K]\), the selected pooled law \(P_{\widetilde\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) is faithful to \(M_k(\widetilde\eta)\). The kernels \(\widetilde\kappa\) are constructed jointly across regimes and need not equal \(\kappa(\eta)\).
statements.justification: A genuine joint kernel construction, rather than graph preservation alone, is required to prove that the replacement specification has a faithful Dai-class realization.
statements.gap: Generic single-DAG faithfulness does not by itself produce one family of selected arm laws whose pooled indicator laws are simultaneously faithful to all replacement regime MAGs.
statements.consumer: It turns each graphical endpoint modification into a statistically well-defined whole-family witness.

statements.statement: For every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and every \(B\) satisfying the admissibility conditions in \(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\), there exists \(\widetilde\eta\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) such that \(A(\widetilde\eta)=A(\eta)\) and \(\mathcal O(\widetilde\eta)=\mathcal O(\eta)=\mathcal O\). Hence \(\widetilde\eta\) has well-defined selected arm laws and faithful pooled laws, preserves every adjacency and every unshielded collider on every full domain \(U_k\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances, and for every \(k\in[K]\) satisfies \(Z_k=T_k(\widetilde\eta)\cup((F_k(\widetilde\eta)\setminus T_k(\widetilde\eta))\cap A(\widetilde\eta))\). No equality between \(\kappa(\widetilde\eta)\) and \(\kappa(\eta)\) is required.
statements.justification: This synthesis theorem supplies a fully specified replacement model with the same complete oracle signature and ancestral selected set.
statements.gap: Published equivalence results do not prove existence of faithful selected-law realizations for a synchronized replacement specification.
statements.consumer: It supplies valid whole-family witnesses for selected-selected circles in the sciPlex2 graph.

statements.statement: There exists a finite-alphabet model \(\eta^\dagger\in\mathfrak M_{3,1}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) whose graph and target data equal \(\mathsf G_{\mathrm{san}}\). For every such faithful model, \(A(\eta^\dagger)=\{1,2\}\), \(Z_1=\{3\}\), and Dai et al.'s retained-edge result gives \(1\to2\) in \(M_1(\eta^\dagger)\). Consequently, the endpoint at vertex \(2\) on that retained adjacency is an arrowhead although \(2\notin Z_1\). The corrected endpoint frontier therefore makes its arrowhead equivalence only for intervention-created adjacencies \(uv\notin H\); it makes no target-membership equivalence for retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\).
statements.justification: The explicit three-variable reduction separates retained basal orientation from the target-driven orientation mechanism and removes the failed normalization.
statements.gap: Dai et al.'s Lemma 6 supplies retained-edge semantics; the earlier draft incorrectly applied the intervention-created-edge target criterion to this distinct case.
statements.consumer: It gives an executable unit check for any implementation of the fixed-selected-set endpoint frontier.

statements.statement: For every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), where the interventional components of \(\mathcal O\) are induced by the faithful pooled selected laws \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), fix \(k\in[K]\) and an intervention-created observed adjacency \(uv\) with \(u,v\in A(\eta)\), meaning that \(uv\) is absent from the observational skeleton \(H\) and present in the regime-\(k\) skeleton. Over \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\), an arrowhead at \(u\) on \(uv\) is feasible if and only if \(u\in Z_k\), and a tail at \(u\) is feasible if and only if \(u\notin Z_k\) or \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\). Here \(u\in Z_k\) means that \(u\) is either a direct target or an indirectly affected ancestrally selected variable, not that \(u\in T_k(\eta)\). Every feasible mark is attained by a whole-family common-basal model in \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\) preserving the full pooled-law signatures on \(U_k\). Retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\) are outside this target-membership equivalence and retain any arrowheads supplied by basal directed structure, as in \(\mathrm{prop:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}reduction}\).
statements.justification: The theorem gives the exact target-and-reachability frontier for the intervention-created selected adjacencies to which that mechanism applies.
statements.gap: The endpoint formulas in Dai et al. give necessary semantics for a fixed model; they do not prove the reverse common-basal witness construction over an equivalence fiber.
statements.consumer: The result classifies which intervention-created selected-gene endpoints can remain biological ambiguity after selection membership is certified.

statements.statement: For every \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), with \(\mathcal O=\mathcal O(\eta)\) formed from the faithful pooled selected laws \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), if \(uv\) is absent from the observational skeleton \(H\) and present in an observed intervention-regime skeleton, then \(u,v\in A(\eta)\).
statements.justification: Dai et al.'s Lemma 4 supplies the initial visible-selectedness certificate used by the rule handle.
statements.gap: This is an imported published lemma and carries no novelty claim; the new issue is closure of partially certified selection membership.
statements.consumer: It initializes cross-regime selectedness without analyst-supplied labels.

statements.statement: For every \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), with \(\mathcal O=\mathcal O(\eta)\) formed from the faithful pooled selected laws \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), the entirely observable closure satisfies \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\subseteq A(\eta)\). The seed inclusion is Dai et al.'s intervention-created-adjacency certificate. At each recursive step, if \(i,j\in\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\) are the nonadjacent endpoints of an observational unshielded noncollider \(i-x-j\), then \(x\in A(\eta)\), so adjoining \(x\) preserves the inclusion.
statements.justification: This theorem turns the noncollider closure into an observable sound certificate set that can legally appear in rule premises.
statements.gap: Dai et al.'s Lemma 4 provides the cross-regime seed but does not state this noncollider closure; Wang, Du, and Zhou instead take singleton background knowledge as supplied.
statements.consumer: It supplies the model-free selectedness predicate used by the local calculus while reserving \(A(\eta)\) for completeness witnesses.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf{Hdl}_{\mathrm{SI}}\), derive a finite rule list \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\), independent of \(D\) and \(K\), whose premises use only the full signature \(\mathcal O\), current endpoint marks, \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\), and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{\mathrm{cert},\mathcal O}\), and determine whether its saturation has the following extension property. For every compatible full signature \(\mathcal O\) obtained from faithful pooled selected laws on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) and every residual reported circle endpoint \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\), there are \(\eta_{\mathtt{tail}},\eta_{\mathtt{arrow}}\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) with opposite marks at \(e\), each a fully specified model generated by one basal selected DAG on \(V\cup S\) and one jointly constructed kernel family satisfying non-target kernel stability across all regimes, while agreeing with every observed mark fixed by saturation and preserving every adjacency and every unshielded collider on each \(U_k\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances. Each witness supplies \(P_{\eta_\star,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), not a single-arm surrogate, as the faithful law of the preserved regime MAG. For each witness \(\eta_\star\) and each regime \(k\), it must realize \(Z_k=T_k(\eta_\star)\cup((F_k(\eta_\star)\setminus T_k(\eta_\star))\cap A(\eta_\star))\), handling direct targets and indirectly affected ancestrally selected variables separately rather than setting \(T_k(\eta_\star)=Z_k\). The proof may use \(A(\eta_\star)\) and \(L_{A(\eta_\star)}\) after a witness has been chosen, but the rule system may neither guess these latent objects nor invoke a global realizability query.
statements.justification: This is the genuine unresolved step between conditional selected-set witnesses and a complete observable local calculus.
statements.gap: No opened paper lifts residual-circle representatives through unknown selection membership and a common exterior DAG completion.
statements.consumer: A positive answer certifies every circle in Dai et al.'s A549 analysis; a negative answer gives a concrete obstruction requiring a richer equivalence-class representation.

statements.statement: There exists a single finite \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\), with rule schemata independent of \(D\) and \(K\), such that for every \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O(\eta))=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O(\eta))\) on \(\mathcal E(\mathcal O(\eta))\). The input \(\mathcal O(\eta)\) is the full collection of regime-MAG adjacencies and unshielded colliders on \(U_k\), where every \(k\in[K]\) regime MAG is the faithful graphical law of \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances, while the equality reports observed endpoints. Equivalently, the rules are sound and every reported endpoint left circular has both a tail and an arrowhead whole-family realization in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O(\eta))\), with each realization a fully specified model sharing one basal selected DAG on \(V\cup S\) across its regimes, carrying its own kernel family with unchanged non-target kernels, supplying its own faithful pooled selected laws, and preserving the entire full-regime signature.
statements.justification: Equality with the canonical endpoint invariant is the theorem-level structure-identification kernel.
statements.gap: Dai et al. prove soundness only, while Zhou and Kocaoglu require enumeration even with known targets and without pre-treatment selection.
statements.consumer: The theorem makes a retained A549 circle an identified equivalence-class feature rather than evidence of an unfinished orientation algorithm.

statements.statement: Fix \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\). If every rule premise and path predicate is decidable uniformly in time polynomial in \(D\), \(K\), and the encoding length of \(\mathcal O\), and every conclusion changes a reported circle endpoint once to a tail or arrowhead, then saturation makes at most \(2(K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates and computes \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\) in polynomial time. The complete skeletons and unshielded-collider families on \(U_k\), with every paired component interpreted as a faithful pooled selected-law signature, including all indicator adjacencies and indicator-involving unshielded colliders, remain immutable inputs. If additionally \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\), this polynomial output is the canonical SI-PAG and no enumeration of \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) is required.
statements.justification: This conditional closure-accounting corollary records the computational consequence of a fixed finite grammar and one-way endpoint updates.
statements.gap: The proposition is not an independent novelty claim; its substantive identification content comes entirely from the complete-calculus theorem.
statements.consumer: An implementation can audit rule-predicate complexity before using complete saturation on a perturbation panel.

statements.statement: Fix \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), let \(\mathcal O=\mathcal O(\eta)\), suppose \(\mathcal Q\neq\varnothing\), and let \(\alpha_q=\beta_q=\alpha/(2|\mathcal Q|)\). Every comparison-\(k\) query family is interpreted under the pooled selected law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\), with arms \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid\zeta_k=0,S^*=\mathbf 1)\) and \(P_{\eta}^{(k)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid\zeta_k=1,S^*=\mathbf 1)\); arm-CI queries are its conditional slices, and neither arm law is separately assumed faithful. For finite query tables with at most \(a_{\max}\) cells, there is a constant \(C_{a_{\max}}<\infty\) such that, if \(B_{\mathrm{mc}}\ge\max\{4(1-\alpha_q)\alpha_q^{-1},8\alpha_q^{-2}\log(4\beta_q^{-1})\}\) and \(\min_{0\le j\le K} n_j\ge C_{a_{\max}}p_{\min}^{-1}\Delta^{-2}\log(2|\mathcal Q|/\alpha)\), then \(\Pr(\mathsf E_{\mathcal Q})\ge1-\alpha\). On \(\mathsf E_{\mathcal Q}\), \(\widehat{\mathcal O}=\mathcal O(\eta)\) for the observational signature and every pooled-law full-regime skeleton and unshielded-collider input on \(U_k\), including every indicator adjacency and every indicator-involving unshielded collider; therefore \(\Pr\{\widehat{\mathcal P}_{\mathrm{conf}}(e)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O(\eta))(e)\text{ for all }e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O(\eta))\}\ge1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: This subordinate inference result transfers one uniformly correct query event through the deterministic complete calculus despite adaptive orientation propagation.
statements.gap: Colombo et al. give asymptotic FCI consistency and Peters et al. give confidence parent sets, but neither gives finite-sample common-basal SI-PAG endpoint coverage.
statements.consumer: A549 users can report only regulatory and selection endpoints supported at a stated familywise confidence level.

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling within and across \(K+1\) arms induced by a fully specified common-basal model. Its local kernels factor over \(G_0(\eta)\), and \(\kappa_v^{(k)}(\eta)=\kappa_v^{(0)}(\eta)\) whenever \(v\notin T_k(\eta)\). For each \(k\in[K]\), the observational and \(k\)-th intervention samples are combined with equal arm weight into \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\); interventions are passively observed and their targets are unknown.
sampling_model.units: Each unit is one draw of the finite-alphabet vector \(X\) conditional on the common pre-treatment selection event \(S^*=\mathbf 1\), which has positive model probability. The pairwise pooled record appends \(\zeta_k=0\) to an observational draw or \(\zeta_k=1\) to a regime \(k\) draw.
sampling_model.treatment: Regime membership is observed through \(k\in\{0,\ldots,K\}\); the node-level direct-target set \(T_k(\eta)\) is latent and need not equal the observed indicator-neighbor set \(Z_k\).
sampling_model.overlap: The technical queried-stratum mass condition \(\min_{(q,w)\in\mathcal I_{\mathcal Q}}\rho(q,w)\ge p_{\min}>0\) is maintained separately from faithfulness and query separation.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each query uses \(\ell_1\) distance to its finite-table null. Arm-CI queries are conditional slices of the pooled selected laws and use within-conditioning-stratum Monte Carlo permutation calibration. Indicator queries are conditional-independence statements under \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), equivalently selected-law conditional invariances, and use simultaneous multinomial bands. The uniform event \(\mathsf E_{\mathcal Q}\) recovers every adjacency and every unshielded collider in each full regime MAG on \(U_k\), including indicator adjacencies and indicator-involving unshielded colliders, before deterministic closure of reported observed endpoints.

estimand_functional: \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O):\ \mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=m\iff\mu_\eta(e)=m\text{ for every }\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O);\text{ otherwise }\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: We show that CDIS is sound, but we conjecture its completeness.
The FCI algorithm is shown to be complete.
We introduce an enumeration-based completion procedure that is sound and theoretically complete.
We present the first polynomial-delay MAG listing method.
We prove consistency of FCI and RFCI in sparse high-dimensional settings.
This approach yields valid confidence intervals for the causal relationships in quite general scenarios.
We develop a provably sound and complete algorithm, F-FCI, using both observational and interventional data.
We provide a graph-theoretic characterization of such rank constraints.

tldr: Selection before perturbation couples every regime-specific MAG through one fully specified model \(\eta=(S,G_0(\eta),(T_k(\eta))_{k=1}^{K},(\kappa^{(j)}(\eta))_{j=0}^{K})\), so ordinary FCI completion in each regime does not reveal all common observed-endpoint information. The central result is a fixed finite within-regime and cross-regime rule calculus whose monotone closure equals the canonical observed-endpoint SI-PAG for Dai et al.'s causally sufficient unknown-target twin-graph class, with comparison \(k\) represented by the pooled selected law of \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) and the compatibility fiber fixed by every adjacency and every unshielded collider in its full regime MAG on \(U_k\). A graphical selected-subgraph specification and a separate simultaneous faithful-kernel realization lemma provide opposing witnesses for intervention-created adjacencies conditional on \(A(\eta)\); retained basal adjacencies are separated by an explicit three-variable sanity reduction. The rule handle computes \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\) and \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}(\mathcal O)\) from oracle-visible predicates, while \(A(\eta)\) appears only in witness proofs. The open mathematical step is to lift those witnesses through unknown selection membership and common exterior completions. A fixed grammar with uniformly polynomial premise and path predicates yields polynomial saturation as a conditional algorithmic corollary, and the completed calculus supports a subordinate simultaneous finite-alphabet confidence SI-PAG. At \(K=0\), the elementary Dai-image inclusion is retained only as a boundary remark informed by Zhang's PAG completeness result.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. prove soundness but leave completeness and an equivalence-class graph open. Single-PAG completeness does not enforce common-basal realizability, and the closest interventional completeness result uses enumeration under known targets without pre-treatment selection.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a local endpoint calculus that is simultaneously dimension independent, regime-count independent, common-basal, unknown-target, and selection aware.
project_justification.fill: The project combines the complete pooled-law regime-MAG adjacency and unshielded-collider signature, including indicator-involving v-structures, with Dai et al.'s visible-selectedness seed, a new observable noncollider closure, certified signature-monotone path propagation, a graphical replacement specification, and a separate simultaneous faithful-kernel realization theorem. The fixed-selected-set frontier is restricted to intervention-created adjacencies, with retained basal edges checked separately. The project then proves residual-circle witnesses and transfers uniform finite-alphabet test accuracy through the complete closure.

related_work: Dai et al., Definition 1, represent comparison \(k\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\), with selected arms \(p(X\mid\zeta_k=0,S^*=\mathbf 1)\) and \(p(X\mid\zeta_k=1,S^*=\mathbf 1)\); their Theorem 1 relates conditional independences of this pooled law to twin-graph separation. Their Theorem 2 defines equivalence by all adjacencies and all v-structures in every regime MAG, their Lemma 4 gives the intervention-created-adjacency selectedness certificate imported here, and their Lemma 5 separates direct targets from indirectly affected ancestrally selected indicator neighbors. They prove CDIS soundness but leave completeness open. Zhang supplies the proof template for finite endpoint-rule completeness over the unrestricted observational MAG fiber; the elementary \(K=0\) inclusion of the Dai image in that fiber is used only as a boundary check, not a theorem contribution. Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes supply ordered-collider invariants for the graphical replacement lemma, but a separate joint kernel construction is still needed to prove the replacement realization fiber nonempty. Zhou and Kocaoglu show that local interventional rules can remain incomplete even with known targets and recover completeness by enumeration. Wang, Du, and Zhou show how opposing representatives under supplied singleton background knowledge support polynomial-delay listing; their complexity result informs only the conditional saturation corollary. Jaber et al. prove unknown-target completeness without selection, confirming that basal-world selection coupling changes the representative construction. Luo et al. develop sound-and-complete F-FCI for interventional discovery with latent confounding and post-treatment selection. Their selection mechanism acts after intervention and their fine-grained interventional fiber is not the pre-treatment common-basal fiber with unknown direct targets studied here, so neither their F-PAG nor F-FCI subsumes the fixed CI/invariance endpoint calculus targeted here. Dai, Qiu, Ng, Dong, Spirtes, and Zhang characterize rank constraints in biased covariance matrices for linear-Gaussian latent-variable models under selection and use them to identify a one-factor model. That rank-constraint regime supplies a complementary source of information about selection and latent structure, whereas the present calculus is restricted to causal sufficiency and uses conditional-independence and cross-regime invariance signatures over a common basal selected DAG. Colombo et al. provide the adjacent uniform graph-learning framework, and Peters et al. provide invariance-based confidence conclusions. Kim et al., Section 2.1, equation (1), use \(\ell_1\), equivalently total variation, distance to the discrete conditional-independence null; their Section 4.2, Algorithm 2 and Theorem 2, establish exact Monte Carlo permutation calibration and preservation of the fixed-alphabet sample-complexity order. These statistical results are used only for the inference rung.
technical_internal_limitation: The replacement theorem conditional on \(A(\eta)\) does not solve the headline problem. \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) is only a graphical specification; graph preservation does not imply that \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) is nonempty or that a pooled selected law is faithful. That nonemptiness requires the simultaneous faithful-kernel lemma, whose new kernels need not equal those of \(\eta\). Beyond fixed \(A(\eta)\), selection membership can vary over \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), an exterior DAG completion must be shared by every regime, and \(Z_k\) identifies only the union of direct targets and indirectly affected ancestrally selected variables. A proof that infers faithfulness from graph preservation, substitutes a single-arm law for \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\), sets \(T_k(\eta)=Z_k\), discards indicator-involving colliders, guesses \(A(\eta)\), uses independent regime completions, or invokes a global basal-DAG enumerator does not establish \(\mathrm{oeq:selection\mbox{-}lifting}\).
honest_scope: The graphical selected-subgraph replacement, simultaneous faithful-kernel realization, synthesized replacement theorem, and intervention-created-edge frontier conditional on \(A(\eta)\) are theorem candidates and remain to be proved against the complete regime-MAG signatures of the pooled selected laws. The retained-edge sanity reduction explicitly shows why basal adjacencies are outside that frontier. The full finite rule list, its unknown-selection-membership lifting lemma, the separate realization of direct and indirectly affected indicator neighbors, and residual-circle witnesses are open and central. Dai et al.'s Lemma 4 supplies only the visible-selectedness seed; the observable noncollider closure and its sound inclusion \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{sel}}(\mathcal O)\subseteq A(\eta)\) are new. Every rule premise uses the observable certificate graph \(L_{\mathrm{cert}}(\mathcal O)\), never the latent graph \(L_{A(\eta)}\). The confidence theorem is conditional on deterministic completeness, pooled twin-graph faithfulness, and the separately maintained queried-stratum mass and query-separation conditions. At \(K=0\), \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{Dai}}(\mathcal O_0)\subseteq\mathcal C_{\mathrm{MAG}}(\mathcal O_0)\) is retained only as a boundary remark: Zhang-compelled marks persist, while equality needs endpoint richness. The proposal excludes latent basal common causes, post-treatment selection, regime-specific selection mechanisms, and failures of pooled twin-graph faithfulness.

threads: Dai et al., Theorems 1--3, give twin-graph CI and invariance semantics; Theorem 2 defines equivalence by all adjacencies and all v-structures in every full regime MAG, including those involving the indicator; Lemma 4 supplies the intervention-created-adjacency selectedness seed; Lemma 5 separates direct targets from indirectly affected ancestrally selected indicator neighbors; and the Conclusion leaves both the equivalence-class representation and completeness open.

Zhang proves a finite sound-and-complete observational PAG rule system. Its tail-completeness construction changes one MAG representative, whereas the first changed step here must synchronize all regime projections through one basal selected model.

Zhou and Kocaoglu's public abstract states that known-target \(\mathcal I\)-FCI is incomplete, that their complete method enumerates compatible MAGs, and that their extra local rules only tighten the output; the proof text was externally inaccessible in this run, and pre-treatment selection and unknown targets are absent.

Wang, Du, and Zhou prove local completeness for singleton background knowledge and polynomial-delay MAG listing. Their result informs the implementation comparison; polynomial saturation here is only the conditional accounting consequence of a fixed grammar with uniformly polynomial predicates.

Luo et al. introduce F-PAG and a sound-and-complete F-FCI algorithm for observational and interventional data with latent confounding and post-treatment selection. Because selection follows treatment and the target equivalence class is a fine-grained post-treatment fiber, this result does not subsume the pre-treatment common-basal, unknown-target CI/invariance calculus.

Dai, Qiu, Ng, Dong, Spirtes, and Zhang give a graph-theoretic characterization of rank constraints in biased covariance matrices for linear-Gaussian latent-variable models and identify a one-factor model under selection bias. Their rank-constraint information and latent-variable target are distinct from the causal-sufficiency, pooled-law CI/invariance signature used here.
literature_map.occupancy_result: No opened source supplies a fixed \(D,K\)-independent rule calculus for unknown-target soft interventions after common pre-treatment selection.

threads: Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes, Theorem 3.7, characterize single-MAG equivalence by adjacencies and colliders with order and prove the criterion through minimal m-connecting paths.

Dai et al., Theorem 2 and Appendix A, reduce twin-class equivalence to all adjacencies and v-structures on the full regime domains \(U_k\), including indicator-involving instances, but do not construct opposing common-basal endpoint witnesses or a simultaneous faithful-kernel realization of a replacement graph; Lemma 5 also prevents identifying direct targets with indicator neighbors.
Zhang's completeness proof constructs representatives for circle marks after closure; it does not preserve intervention descendants or a cross-regime basal fiber.

Wang, Du, and Zhou's Theorem 1 gives opposing MAGs for a residual mark at the vertex receiving singleton background knowledge, but the background knowledge is supplied and only one MAG class is transformed.
literature_map.occupancy_result: No closer paper proves synchronized opposing witnesses for all residual endpoints over Dai et al.'s common-basal fiber.

threads: Colombo et al. prove high-dimensional consistency for FCI and RFCI under sparsity and strong-faithfulness-type separation, but not finite-sample simultaneous endpoint coverage for intervention-coupled PAGs.
Peters, Buehlmann, and Meinshausen invert invariance tests into confidence-valid parent conclusions, but their target is an invariant predictor set rather than an SI-PAG equivalence class.

Kim et al., Section 2.1, equation (1), measure separation by \(\ell_1\) distance to the conditional-independence null, while Section 4.2, Algorithm 2 and Theorem 2, calibrate the UCI statistic by within-stratum Monte Carlo permutations; this supplies query-level decisions rather than graph-level adaptive closure.
Dai et al.'s empirical CDIS analysis has oracle soundness and simulations, without a simultaneous confidence graph.
literature_map.occupancy_result: The exact confidence-SI-PAG target is unoccupied, but its main mathematical value depends on first obtaining the complete deterministic calculus.
